headline: China says avoiding renewed Middle East hostilities is a 'top priority'
dek: Mao Ning: 'The top priority is to avoid the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East that would bring disaster to the region's people.' Beijing will support US-Iran negotiation, a political settlement in Yemen, and 'a proper and comprehensive solution for the opening of the Strait of Hormuz.'…
sources: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning, regular press conference, Beijing, Nov 4; FM Wang Yi meetings in Beijing Nov 2
fault_line: Can Beijing mediate a war it has no military leverage over, or is this summit-season positioning ahead of APEC Shenzhen (Nov 18-19)?

sections.what_happened: Mao Ning: 'The top priority is to avoid the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East that would bring disaster to the region's people.' Beijing will support US-Iran negotiation, a political settlement in Yemen, and 'a proper and comprehensive solution for the opening of the Strait of Hormuz.' Wang Yi met Saudi National Security Adviser Musaad bin Mohammad al-Aiban and Iran's Ali Bagheri Kani in Beijing on Nov 2, urging protection of shipping lanes; China's Middle East envoy will visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia later in November on shuttle diplomacy.
sections.what_verified: CNA and Straits Times report the same FM briefing; note both may carry shared wire copy of one briefing — the primary source is the briefing itself
sections.what_disputed: No commitment, timeline or leverage disclosed: China offers no military alliance or security guarantee in the region (per Seoul Economic Daily analysis), and the envoy trip has no fixed dates. This is positioning, not a mediation outcome. PortWatch note: no new snapshot — latest remains 2026-10-26 file, observation date 2026-10-18 (STALE): 4 Hormuz transits vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day; do not cite as current.
